query: The Shadow Witness {An inkpot has been taken from the professor's desk, on purpose, for the lesson. "The shadows in this room saw who took it," the professor says. "Ask them."|Another staged theft, a quill this time. The professor turns the lamps down. "Shadows remember. They just don't like being asked."|The shadow witness lesson. You know which corner's shadow gossips and which one sulks.} {The lamps burn low and blue.|The shadow under the window is longer than it should be.|{season == "winter": It's dark by mid-afternoon, and the shadows are bold.|A moth keeps throwing huge shadows across the ceiling, confusing everyone.}} Question the long shadow {The long shadow leans toward the door, then toward a third-year's bag. The inkpot is in it. The professor nods. "Good. Shadows point. People lie."|You coax the shadow into showing a hand, a sleeve, a stride. You name the thief; the thief applauds.|The gossiping corner tells you everything before you've finished asking. The professor marks you down for leading the witness, and up for results.} {The shadow stretches toward you instead, and the cold of it settles in your hands. You name the wrong student, confidently.|The shadow shows you a thief who looks a great deal like the professor. The professor finds this very funny; you're freezing.|The sulking corner gives you nothing but chill. You spend the hour with numb fingers and no answer.} Watch the doorway, not the dark {You ignore the shadows and work out who left the room and when. You get the right answer by the wrong method. The professor sighs, but marks it.|You reason it out from the dust on the desk. Correct, and entirely unmagical.|You solve it from the doorway again. The professor has started calling you "the magistrate", and doesn't mean it as a compliment.}
